transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. In the UK, handling refrigerants is illegal for anyone without F-Gas certification, and these kits are ineffective because they do not fix the underlying leak or blockage. The most common cause for this specific symptom pattern on frost-free models is ice blocking the air vents inside due to a defrost failure. Please unplug the appliance and leave both doors open for 24 hours to let all internal ice melt completely. Once you plug it back in, does cooling return? Also, check if there was significant ice buildup on the back wall of the freezer or around the air vents.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok but theres no frost anywhere in the freezer, back wall isnt even cold. so i dont think its ice blocking it? the fridge is at about 13C and freezer around 0C. whats next then

[Heading: Evaporator fan motor failure]
Since there is no ice build-up and the back wall isn't cold, we can rule out a defrost fault blocking airflow. The fact that the fridge (which relies on air circulation from the freezer) is warm while the compressor runs suggests the cooling is being produced in the freezer but not reaching the fridge compartment. The most likely cause now is a failed evaporator fan motor inside the freezer, which pushes cold air into the fridge. If this fan has stopped, the freezer will stay reasonably cold (around 0°C) but the fridge will go warm. Please listen closely inside the freezer with the doors shut. Do you hear the faint hum of a fan running near the back wall, or is it completely silent? This single check separates a simple fan replacement from a more serious sealed-system issue.
yeah i can hear a fan going when the door's shut. so its not that then? compressor is running non stop too and the back of the fridge is only barely warm, not hot like it used to be

[Heading: Sealed system failure (compressor or gas leak)]
This points strongly to a sealed-system fault, such as low refrigerant gas or a failing compressor. As mentioned earlier, I cannot help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit because it involves hazardous pressures and illegal handling of refrigerants without certification. Given these symptoms, DIY kits will not fix the underlying mechanical failure. You need to call a qualified refrigeration engineer to diagnose whether the compressor needs replacing or if the system has a leak.
